Q: CORS cookie not sent in Chrome A:

Chrome is treating this as a cross-site cookie request. withCredentials: true only allows eligible cookies to be sent; it does not override the cookie’s attributes.

For modern Chrome, make sure the cookie is set appropriately, typically:

Set-Cookie: Accounts=...; SameSite=None; Secure

Also keep:

Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://phptest
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true

A preflight is not necessarily expected here because this request can qualify as a “simple” CORS request.

Q: facing oserror: [errno 0] error in kafka python A:

This is usually triggered during an SSL/TLS connection or handshake rather than by Kafka itself. kafka-python has had known cases where Python 3.7 surfaces an SSL failure simply as OSError: [Errno 0] Error.

To reproduce it locally, try running the producer with the same SSL/SASL configuration while repeatedly interrupting the broker connection, restarting the broker, or using an invalid/temporary certificate.

I would first upgrade from Python 3.7 and kafka-python 2.0.2. The project has since added fixes around socket/connection error handling.

Also enable DEBUG logging for kafka.conn and kafka.producer.sender; the lines immediately before the exception should show whether it occurs during DNS, TCP connection, or SSL handshake.

Q: Why is xchg instruction with memory operand always atomic? A:

The atomicity is in the definition rather than in the prefix. With a memory operand, the processor applies its locking protocol for the whole exchange whether or not LOCK is written, so a bare xchg is already an atomic swap because for the xchg, LOCK prefix is implicit, whereus for the other instructions it has to be explicit.

This atomcity costs what any locked read-modify-write costs. On Haswell and Kaby Lake parts, XCHG r,[m] and LOCK ADD [m],r both measure about 17 cycles of latency, roughly five times an unlocked store: measured latencies.

My FastMM4-AVX fork of FastMM4 relies on both halves of that: it takes a lock with a bare xchg and releases it with a plain mov, because only the acquire needs the exchange to be atomic. The locked form buys no faster propagation for that price: nothing pushes a cache line to another core, so a spinning core sees either release when its own load takes the line, on one socket or across several. The single difference is the store buffer, which a locked release drains and a plain store does not, so the plain store can land slightly later when the stores of the critical section are still queued ahead of it. That window is bounded by the buffer, while the LOCK prefix is paid in full on every unlock, upwards of a hundred clock cycles by Agner Fog's measurements, and the buffer behaviour is the one described by x86-TSO. The x86 ordering rules make the plain store safe, which is why the Linux kernel releases a spinlock the same way. So when the release doesn't have to be immedate, the cheaper non-locking release is what I like ;-)

Q: How do I pass the value of a child class to its own child class? A:

It's because the lines of code where you mentioned force_of_friction and force_of_gravity you forgot the self keyword.

For example:

if abs(self.velocity) > 0:
    force_of_friction = (-1)*(self.velocity/abs(self.velocity))*self.mass*abs(self.gravity)
else:
    force_of_friction = vector(0,0,0)
self.add_force(force_of_friction)

force_of_gravity = self.mass * self.gravity

But you tried to use the variable in the child class RotationalMechanics

torque_of_friction = (contact_point - self.position) ^ force_of_friction

torque_of_gravity = (self.position - self.axis_of_rotation) ^ force_of_gravity

When the self keyword isn't used in the variable declaration, the child class will not know of its existence.

I would recommending changing your variable declarations to:

if abs(self.velocity) > 0:
    self.force_of_friction = (-1)*(self.velocity/abs(self.velocity))*self.mass*abs(self.gravity)
else:
    self.force_of_friction = vector(0,0,0)
self.add_force(self.force_of_friction)

self.force_of_gravity = self.mass * self.gravity

Q: Issue pushing to a GitHub repository created with "Initialize repo with a README" option A:

Let's say you have a local repository:

$ git log --oneline
8e7e8d4 hello.txt

The local repository has a single file:

$ ls
hello.txt

Now you create a new repository via the GitHub web interface and initialize it with a README file. At this point, your two repositories have divergent histories. You can add the remote repository to your local repository:

$ git remote add origin git@github.com:larsks/samplerepo.git

But attempting to pull from this repository will yield an error:

$ git pull
warning: no common commits
remote: Counting objects: 3, done.
remote: Total 3 (delta 0), reused 0 (delta 0)
Unpacking objects: 100% (3/3), done.
From github.com:larsks/samplerepo
 * [new branch]      master     -> origin/master
There is no tracking information for the current branch.
Please specify which branch you want to merge with.
See git-pull(1) for details

The important part of this error message is:

There is no tracking information for the current branch.
Please specify which branch you want to merge with.

This is git telling you that while your current branch in your local repository is not associated with any branch in the remote repository, so it doesn't know what to do. You can provide it with a remote branch name explicitly:

$ git pull origin master

This will create a merge commit (and will probably prompt you for a commit message). Once the commit is complete, you can see that the local history now contains both our local commit as well as the commits from the GitHub repository:

$ git log --oneline
7f1231a Merge branch 'master' of github.com:larsks/samplerepo
5f0d62e Initial commit
8e7e8d4 hello.txt

And our working directory now has a merged set of files:

$ ls
hello.txt  README.md

And we can push this to our remote repository. Just typing git push will result in an error similar to what we saw earlier:

$ git push
fatal: The current branch master has no upstream branch.
To push the current branch and set the remote as upstream, use

    git push --set-upstream origin master

So:

$ git push --set-upstream origin master
Counting objects: 6, done.
Delta compression using up to 8 threads.
Compressing objects: 100% (3/3), done.
Writing objects: 100% (5/5), 543 bytes | 0 bytes/s, done.
Total 5 (delta 0), reused 0 (delta 0)
To git@github.com:larsks/samplerepo.git
   5f0d62e..7f1231a  master -> master
Branch master set up to track remote branch master from origin.

And now we're all in sync.

Update: Regarding your questions about --set-upstream:

When you checkout a local branch that matches the name of a remote branch, git will set up the upstream association for you automatically. For example, if the remote repository in this example also had a branch "development", and I did this after adding the remote:

$ git checkout development

I would see:

Branch development set up to track remote branch development from origin.
Switched to a new branch 'development'

On the other hand, if you already have a branch checked out when you add the remote, as in the first part of this example, you need to use --set-upstream to tell git that you want your local branch to track the remote branch.

As an aside, note that there's no requirement that your local branch match the name of a remote branch. You are free to do something like:

git checkout master
git push --set-upstream origin patches

So that from this point on, git push on your master branch will push to the remote patches branch.

Q: How to insert image into into a DOORS attribute A:

I've come across this question, because I had the same problem. Even in 2026. And here's how I accomplished the complex task of inserting an image in IBM DOORS (v9.7):

  1. Select the object you want to insert an image into

  2. Edit object text, not object heading

  3. At the top of DOORS "Insert" -> OLE-Object

  4. A new dialog pops up -> Create new -> "Paintbrush Picture" -> MS Paint opens

  5. In MS Paint at the top left "paste from"

  6. In the file dialog show all image formats and choose your image

  7. Your image should now be visible in MS Paint AND in DOORS

  8. You can now close MS Paint without saving and the image should be inserted in the DOORS object

This worked well for my PNG files.

Q: How to call a SQL Server stored procedure using pymssql from Databricks Serverless Compute? A:

Connect to pymssql

import pymssql

conn = pymssql.connect(server, user, password, db)
cursor = conn.cursor()

The server, user, password, and db strings should be prepared in advance. To prevent handle leak, remember to close the connection:

conn.close()

A Pythonic way to achieve the same effect without the fear of exception interrupting it is this:

with pymssql.connect(server, user, password, db) as conn:
    with conn.cursor() as cursor:
        # ... operations on DB ...

Call stored procedure

With the cursor object created after the connection is established, you can call stored procedure this way:

cursor.callproc(procedure_name, (arg1, arg2 ...))

callproc() expects 2 argument, the first is the stored procedure name, the second is a tuple which contains the arguments. If the stored procedure expects no argument, it should be written this way:

cursor.callproc(procedure_name, ())

And if it expects just 1 argument:

cursor.callproc(procedure_name, (arg1,))

Note that the comma , after arg1 is there to make it a valid tuple.

Reference

See also: pymssql examples - pymssql 2.1.4 documentation

Q: How to make icon show with jpackage if in AppData A:

Icon is set correctly; I’d first check the generated shortcut’s target/icon location under %LocalAppData% rather than the JavaFX app itself. Does the icon also disappear from the Start Menu shortcut, or only the desktop shortcut?

Q: Creating a component through useState used in another useState created component, not working A:

It looks like a stale closure issue. The popup stores subscriptionArea when it’s created, so later state changes won’t update it. Have you tried storing the component/state as data and rendering it inside the popup instead?
